va-county-board-members.area: Virginia — the counties and cities whose current members the state's results cannot settle
va-county-board-members.summary: The Supervisor or Council District card names each member the state's election results settle. For a few seats it names no one and says why, most often a special election the results do not tie to one seat.
va-county-board-members.why: The results list every contest, and a few of them do not say which seat they filled or whose term they finished.
va-county-board-members.wanted: A county's or city's own list of its board or council members. The Department of Elections keeps no list of members appointed to fill vacancies, so an appointee can only come from the county's or city's own page.

va-local-official-contacts.summary: The local district and County or City cards name your supervisors, council members and school board members, and not yet their telephone numbers, e-mail addresses or offices.
va-local-official-contacts.why: The state's election results carry names only, and this app has not yet read each county's and city's own pages for contact details.
va-local-official-contacts.wanted: Nothing from a reader — most counties and cities publish them, and reading them is ours to do.

va-magisterial-district-lines.area: Virginia — the counties whose current election districts differ from the Census Bureau's copy
va-magisterial-district-lines.summary: The Magisterial District card draws the Census Bureau's copy of each county's districts, which in many counties is older than the county's current lines.
va-magisterial-district-lines.why: The Census Bureau's map matches the state's current election districts closely in only about a third of the counties that elect by district.
va-magisterial-district-lines.wanted: Nothing from a reader — the state publishes the current lines, and drawing them here is ours to do.

va-municipal-officeholders.area: Virginia — the towns whose councils the state's results do not settle
va-municipal-officeholders.summary: The City or Town card names every city's council and elected mayor and most towns' mayors. About half of the towns' councils are not named yet, and the card says why for each.
va-municipal-officeholders.why: For those councils the state's results do not settle who sits: a special election filled a seat without saying which, the number of seats on the ballot changed, or the town elects by ward, and this map does not draw its wards.
va-municipal-officeholders.wanted: Nothing from a reader — most towns publish their council members, and reading them is ours to do.

va-school-board-members.area: Virginia — the school boards that are appointed, and the elected seats the state's results cannot settle
va-school-board-members.summary: The School Board District card names each member the state's results settle. A few seats are not named, and where a school board is appointed the County or City card says so and names no one.
va-school-board-members.why: An appointed board is not on any ballot, and a few elected seats' contests do not say which seat they filled.
va-school-board-members.wanted: Each school division's own list of its board members.

va-tribal-government.area: The Rappahannock Tribe's trust land, in King and Queen and Essex counties
va-tribal-government.summary: The Tribal Government card names the councils of two of Virginia's three nations with land, the Pamunkey Indian Tribe and the Mattaponi Tribe, from each nation's own page. It names nobody for the Rappahannock Tribe.
va-tribal-government.why: The Rappahannock Tribe's own site names its chief and no council member, and the state's list of recognized tribes names only the chief and the assistant chief. Part of a council is not shown as if it were all of it.
va-tribal-government.wanted: A list of the Rappahannock Tribe's whole council, from the tribe, that this project may read.
